root.label: State Department restores some global health and humanitarian aid

events.label: State Department restores some global health and humanitarian aid

slots.name: Gavi funding
slots.sentence: Last week, the State Department notified Congress that it would send $600 million to Gavi, the organization that helps low-income countries buy essential childhood immunizations, a year after Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. withdrew American support.

slots.name: total commitments
slots.sentence: It was the latest in a series of financial commitments from the U.S. government to international organizations, working on issues such as hunger and tuberculosis, totaling nearly $2 billion.

slots.name: WFP funding
slots.sentence: $800 million for the World Food Program to fight malnutrition in countries including Ethiopia, Myanmar and Ukraine

slots.name: Unicef funding
slots.sentence: $218 million for Unicef to work improving child health through nutrition, water and sanitation projects

slots.name: Operation End Starvation funding
slots.sentence: $ 100 million to Operation End Starvation , a new public-private partnership working to lower child mortality from malnutrition

slots.name: CEPI funding
slots.sentence: $50 million to the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations for the development of new Ebola vaccines

slots.name: Red Cross funding
slots.sentence: $203 million to the International Committee of the Red Cross and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies for disaster response and humanitarian assistance

slots.name: Global Fund funding
slots.sentence: $661 million to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria, a payment against what was owed from prior year appropriations

slots.name: Ebola response funding
slots.sentence: $220 million for the Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of Congo and $350 million in new humanitarian funding to the affected region, as of June 12
